ios.desc:
Unleash your imagination with Draw Things, the powerful offline AI creation tool for your iPhone or iPad. Create stunning images privately, right on your device – no internet or subscriptions needed for local creation!

• Your Private AI Studio: Create art 100% offline. Your prompts and images stay securely on your device.
• Powerful AI Diffusion Engine: Harness the latest models like SDXL, FLUX.1, Wan 2.2, Qwen Image, Z Image, FLUX.2 and LTX-2.3 for incredible results.
• Pro-Level Control: Master image creation with on-device LoRA training, full ControlNet support, inpainting, outpainting, and pose editing.
• Unlimited Customization: Import your favorite community-made diffusion models and LoRAs effortlessly.
• Free Local Creation: Create limitlessly on your device without ads or token limits. (Optional Cloud Compute available).
• Optimized for Apple: Experience blazing-fast performance, especially on M1, M2, and M3 Apple Silicon Macs. Native support for iPhone, iPad, and Mac.
• Complete Creative Suite: Explore text-to-image, image-to-image, AI video creation, infinite canvas, scribble-to-image, and more.

Perfect for AI enthusiasts, artists, designers, and creators seeking unparalleled control over AI creation. New to AI image / video creation? Dive into our comprehensive Wiki and join our vibrant Discord community for guides, tips, and support!

EULA: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

Privacy Policy: https://drawthings.ai/policy/

quotes.story_title: Stretch iPhone to its limit: 2GiB Stable Diffusion model runs locally on device

quotes.text: iPhones have similar Neural Engine capabilities, obviously far more limited but still quite powerful. You can run some pretty cool DNNs for image generation using e.g. Draw Things app quite quickly: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/draw-things-ai-generation/id6444050820

quotes.text:
https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/ai-photo/id6444911377?mt=12

i’m using this one. pretty good so far. same use of efficient apple stable diff engine.

as well as this monster on mobile:

https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/draw-things-ai-generation/id6444050820

Interesting UI, and great that's it's open-sourced!

M1 Mac owners should also check out the iPad version of Draw Things, which has a large number of features and is in very active development:

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/draw-things-ai-generation/id6444050820

Be aware that there is a bug in macOS 13.2b1 that makes Draw Things unusable on that version of macOS. Hopefully Apple will fix that soon.

The “showing how wasteful their approach to computing resources was” part wouldn’t work on me. I think I no longer see phones as inferior computing resources, at least not that much.

My phone can use ai to generate images locally[1], process video or camera raws, run better games than my laptop and likely more.

[1]: https://apps.apple.com/pl/app/draw-things-ai-generation/id6444050820

quotes.text:
Nobody is deploying 3+GB models to iOS beyond some enthusiast “because you can” apps. Amazing tech but not feasible for any mainstream use yet.

Eg: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6444050820

Comparing the App Store listings, it looks like this app has a much simpler interface and far fewer features than Draw Things. Some users might prefer the simplicity of this app.

(Draw Things is by far the most advanced app that supports on-device Stable Diffusion on iOS devices and Apple Silicon Macs. It had a non-standard UI, but otherwise is really good.)

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/draw-things-ai-generation/id6444050820
